messages.author: a08511b61d1423a7
messages.subject: conditionalPanel based on internal logic
parts:
Hi,
I noticed that all conditionalPanels are based on user input which eventually goes into input$something.
And the condition is tested against input$something.

If I generate a logic inside a reactive function or using a renderText to output$something,
can I use this to create conditionalPanels.
Thanks,
Roy

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: conditionalPanel based on internal logic
parts:
If you assign a reactive (or even just a regular function) to output$something, then yes, you can use output.something in conditionalPanels. However you must also add this line:

outputOptions(output, 'something', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)

messages.subject: Re: conditionalPanel based on internal logic
parts:
Hi Joe,
I still get the same error: Reading objects from shinyoutput object not allowed.
Here is a working example:

#ui.R
library(shiny)
library(reshape)
library(ggplot2)

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(
  headerPanel("Using output$something as internal input"),
  sidebarPanel(
    h4("Text Regular"),
    textOutput('txt1'),
    h4("Text Internal"),
    textOutput('txt2')
    ),
  mainPanel()
  ))

#server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output,session) {
  
output$txt1<-renderText("hello")

fn1<-reactive({
  new<-paste(output$txt1,"again")
  new
})

output$txt2<-renderText(fn1())

#this line doesn't make any difference
outputOptions(output, 'txt1', suspendWhenHidden=FALSE)
})

Thanks,
Roy

messages.subject: Re: conditionalPanel based on internal logic
parts: In server.R, the output object can only have values set on it, they are not readable. If you want to reuse "hello" or whatever logic that is meant to stand in for, create a reactive expression that you use from both output$txt and fn1.
